passages.t: ‘On the day I called, You answered me’
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “Of David” (verse 1). The singer begins with whole-hearted thanks. “I give You thanks with all my heart; before the gods I sing Your praises” (verse 1). “I bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness” (verse 2).

He says why. “On the day I called, You answered me; You emboldened me and strengthened my soul” (verse 3).

Then he looks out to the whole world. “All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O LORD, when they hear the words of Your mouth” (verse 4). “Though the LORD is on high, He attends to the lowly; but the proud He knows from afar” (verse 6).

He ends with trust. “If I walk in the midst of trouble, You preserve me” (verse 7). “The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever” (verse 8). And a last plea: “do not abandon the works of Your hands” (verse 8).
passages.hearers:
Psalm 138 begins the last group of psalms headed ‘of David’, Psalms 138 to 145. The book page explains what such headings may mean.

‘Before the gods’ (verse 1) has been read in more than one way. It may mean in front of the gods of the nations, in open defiance of them. It may mean the heavenly beings around God's throne. Some take it as human rulers. Whichever it is, the singer praises the LORD in the presence of every other power that claims honour.

Israelites who were away from the temple turned toward it to pray. Solomon asked God to hear the prayer “that Your servant prays toward this place” (1 Kings 8:29). Daniel in Babylon prayed with his windows open toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:10).

Verse 6 is a picture of God's ways that runs through the whole Bible. The high God bends close to the lowly, and keeps the proud at a distance.

‘Your loving devotion endures forever’ in verse 8 is the refrain of Psalm 136, now spoken by one person about his own life.
passages.later:
Mary's song says the same as verse 6: God “has scattered those who are proud” and “has exalted the humble” (Luke 1:51-52). James writes, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble” (James 4:6).

Paul's confidence matches verse 8: “He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus” (Philippians 1:6).
passages.asks:
‘You emboldened me and strengthened my soul.’ Sometimes God's answer to prayer is not to remove the trouble, but to give courage inside it. Has that been true for you?

Verse 8 is a prayer you can borrow on any hard day: ‘The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me.’ And when you are not sure of that, pray the last line: ‘do not abandon the works of Your hands.’ You are his work.
